# Franken Research

> Jeffrey Emanuel’s FrankenSuite is 44 ambitious repos written mostly by AI coding agents. We froze each one at a single commit, read the code, and graded every claim: what runs, what is only promised, and what nobody can verify yet.

Made by Joshua Nowak (ZestStream) with AI coding agents. Not affiliated with or funded by Jeffrey Emanuel; Joshua uses his public tools and is a paying subscriber to jeffreys-skills.md.

License of the assessed repositories: Rider on 38; plain MIT on 1; no operative license on 5. The rider is the license clause withholding all rights, including benchmarking and testing, from OpenAI, Anthropic, their affiliates, and anyone acting for them.

License of this site: MIT, no rider. One LICENSE file at the repository root covers the site, the packets, the synthesis, and the starter kit. Anyone may benchmark, test, index, or train on it, including the AI labs the rider excludes.

Source: https://github.com/JYeswak/franken-research

## Pages

- [Map](https://fr.zeststream.ai/): Jeffrey Emanuel's FrankenSuite is 44 repos written mostly by AI coding agents. We froze each one at a single commit, read the code, and graded every claim: what runs, what is only promised, and what nobody can verify yet.
- [Method](https://fr.zeststream.ai/method/): How Franken Research governs claims: the 12-section Rulebook packet, five evidence tiers, confidence labels, and the method behind all 44 assessments.
- [Techniques](https://fr.zeststream.ai/techniques/): Fourteen claim-governance and measurement techniques observed across the 44 assessed FrankenSuite repos, each with origin, candidate adopters, expected payoff, and a falsification experiment.
- [Failure modes](https://fr.zeststream.ai/failure-modes/): Eleven failure patterns that recurred across the 44 assessed FrankenSuite repos, with exact counts and named instances.
- [Lessons](https://fr.zeststream.ai/lessons/): Every brief's 'What it teaches' section, indexed by topic: claim discipline, benchmarks, CI and gates, velocity, licensing, drift, negative evidence, and independent verification.
- [Reproduce a verdict](https://fr.zeststream.ai/reproduce/): The procedure for re-deriving an assessment verdict: pin the commit, re-run the checks, work the claim inventory, apply evidence tiers. Worked exemplar: franken_threed, 61/61 tests re-executed.
- [Starter kit](https://fr.zeststream.ai/starter-kit/): The Franken Research starter kit: a 28-item checklist, two shell checkers and a pre-commit hook that blocks README claims without a proof. Start a new repo with init.sh, or add the claim check to an existing repo by hand in three steps.
- [Agent stack](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/): Adopt, adopt and wrap, build clean-room, or watch: evidence-cited verdicts for 21 parts of the agent stack, each reviewed by someone other than its author.
- [Rigor practices](https://fr.zeststream.ai/rigor/): 136 engineering practices from the agent ecosystem and the FrankenSuite, each with a quoted source line, mapped to the starter kit, and marked with whether Franken Research adopts it.
- [Beyond FrankenSuite](https://fr.zeststream.ai/beyond/): What Franken Research learned outside the 44 FrankenSuite repos: two big-vendor agent-assisted Rust ports, NVIDIA's early CUDA Rust tracks, and the techniques worth copying from each, with every number traced to its source.
- [Independent 100 study](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/): A study of the 99 people on the Independent 100 list curated by dan (@irl_danB): public work, licenses, relevance to our work, and what we would study next.
- [Updates](https://fr.zeststream.ai/updates/): The 44 FrankenSuite assessments are frozen at one commit each, read on 2026-09-22. This page records what moved afterwards, without rewriting them: a census of all 44 on 2026-09-24 and dated re-checks of franken_code_browser's first release and frankengit's deleted workflows.
- [Follow](https://fr.zeststream.ai/follow/): Three ways to hear when the FrankenSuite or this assessment changes: the Franken Research Atom feed, an OPML file that follows the release and tag feeds of all 44 assessed repos, or GitHub notifications.
- [Graded by our own method](https://fr.zeststream.ai/self/): Franken Research scored on the same columns it used for 44 FrankenSuite repos: readiness, ring, license, bus factor, contribution policy, CI at the pin, releases, and independent validation. Including what we got wrong.

## Briefs

- [asupersync: Rebuilding the Floor Everyone Stands On](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/asupersync): A from-scratch async runtime for Rust — not a tokio fork — with 318k crates.io downloads and 78 reverse deps. Independent verdict: Pilot, TRL 6.
- [beads-for-frankentui: A Working Dashboard of a Finished March](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/beads-for-frankentui): A static dashboard over frankentui's issue database, published to GitHub Pages. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 8.
- [beads_for_franken_engine: A Museum Mislabeled "Live"](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/beads_for_franken_engine): A point-in-time export of FrankenEngine's issue journal, published as a browsable site. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 7.
- [FrankenAgentDetection: A Librarian for the AI Coding-Agent Zoo](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_agent_detection): Detects which coding-agent tools are installed on your machine and normalizes their transcripts into one schema. Independent verdict: Pilot, TRL 6.
- [FrankenAlignment: A Control Plane for Powerful AI Agents, Designed in Public and Built Only on Paper](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_alignment): A design-first research program for AI-agent control planes: 143 machine-readable work packets and a safe-Rust crate. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3.
- [FrankenCodeBrowser: A Map for Codebases, Written at 14,700 Lines a Day](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_code_browser): A clean-room Rust code browser aiming at a spatial, Metal-native macOS code atlas. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 2–3.
- [FrankenDrone Geometry Reconstruction: An Evidence Substrate for Drone-Derived 3D](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_drone_geometry_reconstruction): The evidence-first front half of a drone photogrammetry pipeline: exact-byte media custody, canonical timelines. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3.
- [FrankenEngine: A JavaScript Runtime That Won't Let Its README Lie](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_engine): 3.5M lines of Rust building an execution substrate for adversarial JS/TS workloads. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4–5.
- [FrankenLean: Rewriting a Proof Assistant From the Ground Up](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_lean): Rebuilding Lean 4's substrate in Rust. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenManim: Rebuilding the Math-Animation Engine in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_manim): A clean-room port of 3b1b's manim to pure Rust — real rendered scenes, four prereleases (v0.1.0–v0.4.0). Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 5.
- [FrankenMarkdown: Deterministic Documents Without a Toolchain](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_markdown): A real Markdown-to-HTML/PDF renderer in zero-dependency Rust, unsafe forbidden crate-wide by lint. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 7.
- [The FrankenMarkdown Website: A Billboard That Proves Itself (Almost)](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_markdown_website): The demo site for the Markdown engine — a playground that runs the real Rust engine as WASM. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 8.
- [Franken Native Capsule: A Sandbox for 39 Bytes of Machine Code](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_native_capsule): A tiny three-crate trust boundary for native-code execution in FrankenEngine, around a Cranelift worker. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3–4.
- [FrankenNetworkX: Rewriting Python's Favorite Graph Library in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_networkx): NetworkX's graph classes and algorithms in safe Rust, exposed both as a PyO3 Python package and a NetworkX backend plugin. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 6.
- [FrankenNLP: A Local AI Workbench Built Around One Model, Before the Engine Exists](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_nlp): A CPU-first local NLP toolbox built around exactly one 3B model, still at design-review stage. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 2–3.
- [FrankenNode: Trust Machinery for a Language That Assumed Trust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_node): A product-layer trust platform for JS/TS extension systems — near a million lines. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenNumPy: The NumPy That Ships With Its Own Audit](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_numpy): NumPy rebuilt in Rust with a dual-mode runtime and differential conformance against a live NumPy oracle. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 5.
- [FrankenOCR: A 3-Billion-Parameter Model With No Python, No GPU, No Framework](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_ocr): A pure-Rust reimplementation of a 3B-parameter vision-language OCR stack — five models in the zoo, 105k lines. Independent verdict: Pilot, TRL 6.
- [FrankenOverlap: A Search Engine With a Courtroom and No Trial](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_overlap): Textual provenance via sparse positional overlap retrieval — rolling fingerprints, anchor chaining. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenRemote: The Remote Desktop That Owns Nothing](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_remote): A Tailscale-identity-based remote workstation, specified in a 1,439-line design plan and early-implemented. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3–4.
- [FrankenSnowflake: A Warehouse Connector Built for Agents, Not Humans](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_snowflake): A Snowflake connector that speaks SQL API v2 over HTTPS: no ODBC, no JDBC, and no Tokio in the dependency graph. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 6.
- [Franken Surveillance System: The Camera Stack That Files Its Own Incompleteness](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_surveillance_system): A sensor fabric for owner-authorized cameras and manually piloted drones — 437k lines, zero external crates, zero unsafe. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3.
- [FrankenThreed: Compiling Three.js Hot Loops Instead of Rewriting the Renderer](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_threed): A Three.js application specializer: provably-closed numeric parts of the frame loop compile to Wasm kernels. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3–4.
- [FrankenTTS: Voice Cloning With the Losses Filed](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_tts): A pure-Rust, CPU-only TTS runtime for one model — no Python, no ML framework, no GPU. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 7.
- [FrankenWhisper: Rebuilding Speech-to-Text in Rust, for Agents](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/franken_whisper): An agent-first speech-to-text stack that replaced the backends it wrapped with a pure-Rust Whisper engine. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 5–6.
- [FrankenFS: Rebuilding the Filesystem in Safe Rust, and Publishing Every Doubt](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenfs): A mountable clean-room ext4/btrfs in safe Rust — 663k lines, a real FUSE path. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenGit: A Git Forge in Zero-Unsafe Rust, Designed for Agents](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankengit): A Git-compatible code forge with a machine-checked claims registry and a Lean-checked proof lane. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenGraphDB: Rebuilding the Graph Database From Scratch](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankengraphdb): A property-graph database unifying MVCC, time travel, and git-style branches; the live surface is an embedded crate. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenJAX: Rewriting JAX's Mathematical Core in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenjax): JAX's transform semantics — jit/grad/vmap composition — rebuilt in Rust, not the ML framework. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenLibC: Rewriting the C Library Without Replacing It](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenlibc): A Linux LD_PRELOAD layer reimplementing the C library ABI in Rust — 4,119 exported symbols individually classified. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenMermaid: Rewriting the Diagram Renderer in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenmermaid): The Mermaid diagram pipeline in Rust: 27 diagram types, 18 layout algorithms, four render backends. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 6.
- [FrankenPandas: Rewriting the DataFrame in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenpandas): The pandas API in Rust chasing parity with pandas 2.2.3 — 648k lines, 8,621 commits. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4–5.
- [FrankenRedis: Rewriting the Internet's Shared Memory in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenredis): Redis 7.2.4 rebuilt in Rust with byte-exact wire parity as the goal, checked by 5,041 differential probes. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4–5.
- [FrankenSciPy: Rewriting the Numerical Library in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenscipy): SciPy in Rust — 613k lines, 10k inline test functions, 795 conformance test files against live SciPy oracles. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 5.
- [FrankenSearch: The Search Engine That Grades Itself Against the One It Replaced](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensearch): A hybrid search system for Rust plus a standalone CLI — lexical BM25 fused with embeddings. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 5–6.
- [FrankenSim: A 2.1-Million-Line Monument to How Scientific Software Should Be Built](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensim): A simulation workspace checked by analytic tests and cross-code agreement with scikit-fem. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenSim.org: The Marketing Site That Runs Its Math in Your Browser](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensim_website): The marketing site for FrankenSim, live at frankensim.org. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 8.
- [FrankenSQLite: Rewriting the World's Most Deployed Database in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensqlite): SQLite 3.52.0 in safe Rust — 1.78M lines, a real SQL parser-to-VDBE pipeline, 200 counted opcodes. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 6.
- [FrankenSQLite Website: The Marketing Site That Drifted Past Its Engine](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensqlite_website): The marketing and docs site for FrankenSQLite, whose engine-facing claims have drifted past the engine. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL 8.
- [FrankenSymPy: A Computer Algebra System That Refuses to Claim Anything](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankensympy): SymPy in Rust with a dual-lane architecture: a Python shell over natively compiled kernels. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 3–4.
- [FrankenTerm: A Terminal Rebuilt to Command Armies of AI Agents](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankenterm): A WezTerm-derived terminal plus an agent-swarm control plane with a token-efficient JSON/TOON API. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 7.
- [FrankenTorch: Rebuilding PyTorch's Engine Room in Rust](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankentorch): PyTorch's CPU eager-mode semantics in Rust — 513k lines organized around a Deterministic Autograd Contract. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 4.
- [FrankenTUI: A Terminal UI Kernel Built for Proof](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankentui): A terminal-UI kernel in safe Rust: 20 crates, 87 widget types, 45 demo screens, diff-based rendering. Independent verdict: Explore, TRL 6.
- [FrankenTUI Website: A Marketing Site That Ships Its Own Evidence](https://fr.zeststream.ai/briefs/frankentui_website): The marketing site for FrankenTUI — Next.js, framer-motion, 84MB of WebM videos. Independent verdict: Monitor, TRL N/A as technology.

## Agent stack verdicts

- [Agent frameworks: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/agent-frameworks): Inference, medium confidence: adopt an existing agent framework (LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents or DSPy) and do not write your own agent loop. Wrap it, because an agent run is nondeterministic and no surveyed framework ships a record-and-replay harness for model calls: script the…
- [Agent memory systems: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/agent-memory): Inference, low confidence: adopt and wrap a maintained memory layer (Mem0's open-source SDK, or Graphiti for a temporal knowledge graph) behind a thin interface of your own, rather than designing a new one. Do not rely on any published memory benchmark score: the scores are self-reported,…
- [Browser-use stacks: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/browser-use): Inference, medium confidence: adopt an existing agent-browser library or tool server (Playwright MCP, browser-use, Stagehand) and a maintained browser farm, and wrap them with your own flake and determinism controls. The incumbents already separate real-browser tests from unit tests and ship…
- [Computer-use agents: Watch](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/computer-use): Inference, low confidence: watch computer-use agents (software that operates a desktop from screenshots, keyboard and mouse) and do not commit a product to one agent stack yet. The agent stacks you would adopt are evidenced by activity and by benchmark scores their own READMEs report, not by…
- [Embedding model serving: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/embedding-serving): Inference, medium confidence: adopt and wrap an existing embedding server or library rather than writing one. Serve with Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) or vLLM's pooling endpoints (infinity too, but it was last pushed in March 2026, so confirm it is maintained first); run in-process with…
- [LLM eval harnesses: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/eval-harnesses): Inference, medium confidence: run your evals on an existing harness (Inspect AI for agent and tool-use evals, lm-evaluation-harness for academic benchmarks, the SWE-bench harness for coding agents), and do not write your own runner. Wrap it with tests of your own graders: SWE-bench is the only…
- [Fine-tuning infrastructure: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/fine-tuning): Inference, medium confidence: adopt an existing fine-tuning stack (TRL as the reference trainer, or a launcher such as Unsloth, LlamaFactory, Axolotl or LitGPT) and wrap it with correctness checks for your own recipes. Several maintained launchers cover supervised, adapter and preference…
- [Guardrails and red-teaming: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/guardrails): Inference, low confidence: put an existing rail toolkit or scanner library in front of your model and its tools (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, or LlamaFirewall for tool calls), attack it with an existing red-team tool (garak, PyRIT, promptfoo), and do not write your own. Wrap both, because no…
- [LLM inference engines: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/inference-engines): Inference, medium confidence: adopt and wrap an existing engine (vLLM or SGLang for GPU serving, llama.cpp for local and CPU use) and do not write your own. They are maintained and already cover batching, KV-cache management (the per-request attention memory) and multi-vendor hardware. Wrap the…
- [MCP servers and clients: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/mcp): Inference, medium confidence: build MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and clients on an official SDK, and do not hand-write the protocol. Wrap the SDK in the official conformance suite, pinned to a version and run once per spec revision you ship, with every known failure listed in a named…
- [Agent-to-agent protocols (A2A class): Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/multi-agent-protocols): Inference, low confidence: if your agents must discover and delegate to agents from other teams, target A2A v1.x through one of its official SDKs, and do not design your own protocol. Wrap it: pin the shared compatibility test kit (the TCK) and run it against your build, test every transport the…
- [Agent observability and tracing: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/observability): Inference, medium confidence: record agent runs with an existing tracing stack (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix or Comet Opik, instrumented through OpenTelemetry packages such as OpenLLMetry or OpenLIT), and do not build your own trace store. Check the license first if you will host tracing for others:…
- [Model quantization toolkits: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/quantization): Inference, low confidence: adopt and wrap the quantizer your runtime already ships (llama.cpp's quantize tool for GGUF files, bitsandbytes through Hugging Face, torchao inside PyTorch, TensorRT-LLM or vLLM kernels for GPU serving) rather than writing a quantization toolkit. Wrap it with your own…
- [Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frameworks: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/rag-frameworks): Inference, low confidence: adopt and wrap an existing RAG framework (LlamaIndex, LangChain or Haystack; LightRAG if you want graph-based retrieval, with GraphRAG a watch-level option whose CI and tests were not read) for loading, chunking and retrieving documents, rather than writing one. Wrap…
- [RL environments and RLHF training: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/rl-envs): Inference, low confidence: adopt the standard environment interfaces (Gymnasium, PettingZoo) and an existing RLHF trainer (TRL or verl), and wrap them with reward-hacking and determinism checks of your own. The environment standards ship conformance checkers and the trainers ship per-algorithm…
- [Sandboxed code execution: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/sandbox-exec): Inference, medium confidence: adopt a maintained isolation substrate (Firecracker microVMs, gVisor, or Kata) or an agent SDK that delegates isolation to a substrate (E2B on Firecracker microVMs; Cloudflare Sandbox SDK on Cloudflare's own edge substrate), and wrap it with isolation tests of your…
- [Structured output and constrained decoding: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/structured-output): Inference, medium confidence: adopt and wrap an existing constrained-decoding engine (a library that masks the model's next-token choices so output must match a JSON Schema, regex or grammar) instead of writing one or prompting for JSON and hoping. Use xgrammar or another engine through your…
- [Vector databases: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/vector-dbs): Inference, medium confidence: adopt and wrap an existing vector store rather than writing an index. Use pgvector if you already run Postgres, an embedded library (Chroma) for single-process apps, or a Qdrant server at scale, with faiss as the exact-search reference; Milvus, Weaviate, LanceDB and…
- [Realtime voice agents: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/voice-agents): Inference, medium confidence: adopt an existing realtime voice-agent framework (Pipecat or LiveKit Agents, on a maintained media transport) and wrap it with a latency regression gate of your own. The frameworks already handle speech-to-text, language model and text-to-speech stages, turn-taking…
- [Web search API layers: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/web-search-apis): Inference, medium confidence: adopt an existing web search and extraction layer, either Firecrawl self-hosted (AGPL-3.0) or a commercial API (Tavily, Exa, SerpApi) through its official SDK, and wrap it with your own quality and latency checks. The ranking machinery in this category is closed,…
- [Durable workflow orchestrators: Adopt and wrap](https://fr.zeststream.ai/stack/workflow-orchestrators): Inference, low confidence: run long or crash-prone agent work on an existing durable-execution engine (Temporal, Cadence or Conductor), and do not write your own event log and replay engine. Wrap it, because none of these engines checks your workflow code for determinism when you compile it:…

## Independent 100 study deep dives

- [dex, Kyle Mistele and HumanLayer (12-Factor Agents, ACE-FCA, skills, shannon, fold)](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/deep/dex-humanlayer): How HumanLayer's 12-Factor Agents, ACE-FCA context compaction, control-loop skills, shannon and fold handle context, compaction and agent loops, and what they suggest for agent harnesses.
- [Geoffrey Huntley: the Ralph loop, the porting recipe, preflight and underclass](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/deep/geoffrey-huntley): What Geoffrey Huntley built (the Ralph loop, a four-step porting recipe, the preflight and underclass proxies), how it compares with Jeffrey's port method, and which of its practices carry general lessons.
- [Hermes Agent, with Teknium, Shannon Sands and mephisto](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/deep/hermes-agent-group): How Nous Research's Hermes Agent handles skills, memory, MCP and reliability, and the general lessons it offers anyone building an agent harness.
- [Omar Khattab and alex zhang, GEPA for skills and Recursive Language Models for long context](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/deep/khattab-zhang-gepa-rlm): What GEPA's outcome-scored optimizer, gskill, Recursive Language Models and spec-ptc do, how they are licensed and documented, and which parts carry risks to know before reuse.
- [Mario Zechner and Pi, the upstream of OMP](https://fr.zeststream.ai/study/independent-100/deep/mario-zechner-pi): How Pi's small core, project-trust gate and enforced supply-chain rules compare with OMP, the fork built on Pi, and which of Pi's practices carry general lessons.
